# Brad Lasater

> Applied scientist and machine-learning engineer with ten years of production
> ML, forecasting, optimisation, and state-estimation work across consumer
> marketplaces, live events, aerospace, and defense, owning the full lifecycle
> from research design and point-in-time data pipelines through deployment,
> calibration, and monitoring. His current research applies that same
> research-to-production discipline to systematic volatility: an end-to-end
> research and execution platform for defined-risk SPY and SPX/SPXW structures
> at roughly 5-45 days to expiry, with VIX options captured for the term
> structure, documented in public including the parts that do not work. Based
> in the United States, pursuing quantitative research,
> research-engineering, and quantitative developer roles in New York.

Brad Lasater holds U.S. Patent 10,204,323, was previously cleared TS/SCI, and
served as a Sergeant and instructor in the United States Marine Corps before
his technical career. He holds an M.Eng. in Systems Engineering from Arizona
State University and a B.S. in Applied Mathematics from the University of Texas
at Arlington.

The volatility platform is early. The ingest, warehouse and pricing layers run:
options chains, trades and day bars land on a schedule under a daily coverage
audit, implied volatility is inverted per contract with own Greeks and checked
each evening against put-call parity and reprice identities, and those are
reduced to an ATM implied-volatility term structure — one row per date, root and
expiry, back to 2022-08-31 — with the forward recovered from put-call parity
because no index level is entitled on this data tier. On top of that curve a
raw-SVI (Gatheral) smile is fitted per expiry over OTM strikes for SPX and SPXW,
with butterfly and calendar arbitrage repaired inside the fit rather than
checked afterwards; SPY is refused because its strikes are American and would
invert under the wrong exercise boundary. A HAR-RV baseline realised-variance
forecast is implemented and tested but not yet scheduled or evaluated out of
sample. Every stage downstream of that — sizing, risk authorisation, execution —
is designed and not built.

The target architecture, none of which yet runs: it estimates physical variance,
extracts the market's risk-neutral
variance, trades only when the variance risk premium exceeds modelled costs and
uncertainty, and sizes the resulting exposure under explicit Greek and drawdown
constraints. Its distinguishing feature is not the returns —
which may not exist — but the research process: an evaluation protocol fixed in
public before any results were produced, deflated Sharpe ratios reported next to
raw ones, execution costs modelled rather than assumed away, and an append-only
live record enforced by CI rather than asserted. The work draws
on Euan Sinclair on the mechanics and economics of volatility trading, and
Marcos López de Prado on the statistics of not fooling yourself.

## Core pages

- [Home](https://bradlasater.com/): Who Brad Lasater is, selected experience at Nift, Ticketmaster, Lockheed Martin, and Boeing, and the through-line connecting them — decision-making under uncertainty.
- [The volatility system](https://bradlasater.com/vol/): The architecture stage by stage, each labelled with its current implementation status. Phase 1 trades defined-risk SPY and SPX/SPXW structures at roughly 5-45 days to expiry, with VIX options captured for the term structure: point-in-time data and cleaning, arbitrage-free surface construction, volatility forecasting, signal and sizing, risk and hedging, execution, evaluation, and operations.
- [Evaluation protocol](https://bradlasater.com/vol/methodology.html): The pre-committed rules for judging the platform — purged and embargoed cross-validation, mandatory baselines that must be beaten, cost and friction modelling, deflated performance statistics, and kill criteria fixed in advance.
- [Build status and live record](https://bradlasater.com/vol/track-record.html): Append-only out-of-sample results. Tracking has not started yet. Every observation is a separate dated commit; CI rejects any edit to published history; every statistic is recomputed in the browser from the raw data.
- [System handbook](https://bradlasater.com/handbook/): The engineering documentation for the running data-ingest and pricing box the platform is built on — repository layout, data flow, the ingest jobs and the vendor constraints they work around, the market-data and pricing layers, the warehouse-to-math boundary, the daily canary, desk conventions, and the operational state of the machine itself. Status chips mark what is shipped, what is write-only, and what is not built yet, so design intent is never mistaken for running code.
- [Research log](https://bradlasater.com/log/): Dated entries on what was tried, what was expected, what happened, and what was wrong. Negative results are entries too.
- [Curriculum vitae](https://bradlasater.com/cv.html): Full professional history including military and teaching service, education, patents, and technologies.

## Research log entries

- [Every price in this system is a traded price, and that changes which tests are even meaningful](https://bradlasater.com/log/2026-09-07-pricing-with-imperfect-market-inputs.html): Option NBBO is a 403 on this data tier, so implied volatility is inverted from last trade or day close rather than from a quote midpoint. The consequence is not merely noisier numbers — it invalidates one of the three daily identity checks whenever either leg of a pair is a stale print, and it makes the spread-based cost model uncalibratable rather than approximate. (published 2026-09-07)
- [Half my datasets can be backfilled and half cannot, and that decides what a replay may claim](https://bradlasater.com/log/2026-09-07-historical-completeness-vs-point-in-time.html): Option day bars reach back to 2022-08-31 and can be rebuilt from the vendor archive at any time; chain snapshots exist only from 2026-08-31 because there is no historical snapshot endpoint. That asymmetry, not storage cost, is what limits which backtests this system will ever be allowed to run. (published 2026-09-07)
- [The ATM term structure agrees with itself by construction, so I had to work out when its agreement is evidence](https://bradlasater.com/log/2026-09-07-atm-term-structure-before-a-surface.html): The term structure inverts both the call and the put at the at-the-money strike and writes out both. When put-call parity happens to select that same strike, the two legs invert to identical volatilities as an algebraic identity — so their agreement proves nothing, and only the dates where the two strikes differ carry information. (published 2026-09-07)
